I've farmed this land for 55 years, so I know what it needs. Let me think through each crop.

**Winter wheat (planted last October, harvest this June):** I already put the seed in the ground, so the big decisions for this season are topdressing and irrigation. I planted Jimai 22, an improved variety — everyone in our village uses it, reliable, around 500 kg/mu in a normal year. Base fertilizer went in at planting, about 40 kg of compound 15-15-15 plus 20 kg urea per mu. Come green-up in March, I topdress 15 kg urea per mu with the irrigation. Then another 10 kg at jointing if the crop looks pale. Total N works out to around 18 kg/mu — our soil here is not poor but wheat needs it. I irrigate three times: winter water in December (already done), green-up in March, and jointing-booting in April. If May is dry I add one more at grain-fill. Spray twice: once for aphids and powdery mildew around booting, once closer to heading for wheat midge. Quzhou has had fusarium head blight risk the last few wet springs, so I keep tebuconazole ready.

**Summer maize (plant right after wheat harvest in June):** I plant Zhengdan 958 or Denghai 605, hybrid — no one plants traditional maize anymore, yield would be half. I do no-tillage direct seeding into the wheat stubble, it saves two days and keeps moisture. About 4,500 plants per mu. Fertilizer: 30 kg compound at sowing, then 20 kg urea side-dressed at the big trumpet stage (V10-V12). That gives about 18 kg N/mu. I irrigate once at sowing if June is dry, and once more at tasseling if needed — the well is reliable, but electricity is not free. Spray once for corn borer around tasseling, sometimes twice if armyworm shows up. Expected yield 600 kg/mu, I've been hitting that most years.

**Cotton (2 mu on the sandy corner):** Cotton has become less profitable and I only keep a small plot because that piece of land drains too fast for good wheat. Bt hybrid seed. I plough that plot — cotton likes loose soil. Base fertilizer: 25 kg compound plus 10 kg urea. Then topdress 15 kg urea at squaring and another 10 kg at flowering. Less N than you'd think because too much N makes it grow tall and hollow. Potassium matters more — I add 10 kg potassium sulfate. Irrigate 2-3 times, spray 5-6 times through the season — bollworm, aphids, spider mites. Yield around 250 kg seed cotton per mu, nothing like the old days.

Allocation: 5 mu wheat-maize rotation on the main fields, 2 mu cotton. Wait — I have 12 mu total, so wheat-maize on 10 mu, cotton on 2 mu.
